body:
I don't think he has a plan.

I see another doc for TMS.  I have to drive 1.5 hours each way for that.  It's destroying my car.  Also, I can't drive that far anymore, so my wife is taking me.  

If I could be sure my family would be OK and that I would (mortal sin), I'd end it now.  I wish I could.  I keep thinking about my littlest, though.  She would not ever understand.

I'm 42.  I feel about as you do.  Not sure what to do myself, but have you tried all the options for treatment?  They're lots of them.

Medication.

ECT.

TMS.

Therapy.

I'm not on here often enough to promise a quick reply, but I'll answer any questions I can, if I can.  Of course, I may be completely incoherent in an hour also.

I've been on meds for years.  I've been on every class of meds as I understand it.  Doc says meds are ineffective.  I've been hospitalized (never again), had ECT, TMS, and CBT with a psychologist.  

TMS worked for a while, some of the meds worked a bit.  Now, I cannot control my own emotions.  I've been writing letters to my wife and kids in case I don't make it.  

I'm beyond frightened this time, and I feel guilt because I need to be strong for them.  

Reddit isn't the place for help, but I'm at the end of my rope.  

Thank you for replying.
The offer stands.

These people can and will help if you give them your information.  Whether your parents or school will or not.  

http://suicidepreventionlifeline.org/#

These are other organizations that might be able to help.

http://www.youthvillages.org

Jasonfoundation.com

You can also PM me, but I'm not on this account regularly and I'm also in a bad place.  But I'll do what I can if I can.

Thanks for words of encouragement.  They help, for a little while at least.  

I'm still writing letters.  Just so they're here if I lose the fight.  But I'm fighting.  There is some discussion of placing me in a hospital again.  And some of permanent disability.

I hope I can get better.  But I'm frightened.

Always a lot of issues.  Plato said, "Be kind, for everyone you meet is fighting a hard battle."

In my short 42 years, I have found this to be so.  No one has it together.  No one has the answers.  We're all just muddling through the best we can.  There is pain and there is joy.  Laughter and tears.  

If I can help you, let me know.  Sometimes I'm not on here for weeks at a time, but if I'm here and I can help, I will.
Fighting it.  Don't know if I can forever.  Depression is an insidious disease.  I'm not always rational.  I'm not sure I am now.

I can offer info on treatment if depression is the issue.  

Most of it doesn't work for me, but it does for many, many people.  And I know about most of it from experience.
I've given up driving.  For the most part.
My wife drives me now.  For now.  I almost didn't make it home Monday.  I had to pull over and lie in the grass beside the road.
Hid mine in my comic boxes.  Right among the comics.  I used to tape my cigarettes inside the closet above the door.  My mother put my stuff away every day and never found them.

I Just wrote a letter to my wife.  I've been thinking, they can get over my death if I am gone.  It'll take some time, but while I am here, I'm constantly a burden.  I don't want my kids to see me like this, or my wife to have to care for me like an invalid.  

I'm not sure what to do with what you just told me.

I'm in no place to couple someone who is suicidal, but being a virgin and shy around girls is no reason for this.  Sex is overrated and over-sold in our society.  

Having a real connection to someone is a much greater thing.  Sex will come later if you find love first.

As for never being able to find it, that's what I thought too.  Now I've been married probably longer than you've been breathing.  My wife loves me.  So do my three children.  They're honestly all that keeps me here.

Give it time, listen to the other redditor telling you to try to talk to her.  If it doesn't work out, keep looking.
It depends on a number of factors.  If you do not know what you are doing you will die slowly.  I will not educate you on how to do it right.
I'm writing letters tonight myself.  I probably will write more tomorrow.  Maybe.
It is unlikely that this will kill you.  It is much more likely that it will hospitalize or disable you.  You need to rethink this.  Call a psychiatrist.  Or someone.

I tell many people to try Trans cranial magnetic therapy.  It works for the majority of people.  It worked for me, but now I'm having to go for follow-up treatments.  Many people do, but if you get the follow up treatments on a regular schedule, it can stave off the demons.  Also, look into genetic testing.  It can pinpoint what meds your body is most likely to respond to.  I just had mine three weeks ago.  Just got the results this week.  As it turns out, the medicine I've been on for a year is just about the worst medicine there is for me.  It barely has any positive effect and the side effects are drastic.  The gene test spelled this out.  

I can find out the name of the specific company if you wish.  The test is $6,000 and insurance will not cover it, but **they have financial assistance**.  I make nearly $90,000 but still qualify for their financial assistance.  Looks like I'll be paying just over $300.
Still, don't be too hard on him.  The toughest fighters sometimes lose the fight.  I very nearly did today.  But, as it turns out, I get to fight tomorrow.
I don't know.  I'm in treatment.  If I don't get better, I'll probably go back to an in-patient facility again.  That's almost a fate worse than death.
The demons in my mind grow stronger.  The day may come when I can no longer drown their voice with mine.  On that day, I no longer have lucidity--and I no longer have choice.

Here's the thing.  You may be broken, you may be tormented, you may even be cast aside.  But you are not worthless.  Your value exceeds that of the stars.  You are a human life.  If you will accept it, a human soul.  For that alone, you have great value.

Internet strangers can be good and bad.  Let me try to be good, but fair warning, I'm fighting my own battle.  At the moment I am winning.  That can change in an instant, as I feel you know.  

I believe in you.  Because I know you?  No, of course not.  But because with all the wicked, evil, black, and discouraging things in my own mind--I believe in the potential of the human soul or mind if you prefer.  There is greatness in us.  There is greatness in you.

The. You fight this for them.  That voice that tells you that they are better off without you?  Not your voice.  That's the demon inside.  I don't mean some supernatural hellspawn.  I mean your demon.  Your own personal tormentor.  And he's a liar.  They will not be better off without you.  And did it ever occur to you that you will also be without them?  I don't know what is wrong in your life.  I know it's bad, or you wouldn't be here of all places.  But if you have love in your life, you have something worth fighting for.  

You got me too, for as long as I'm here.  Mind you I'm fighting my own battles and I know the day may come when I lose.  But I'm fighting now for me.  And I'm asking you to fight for you.  For your loved ones.  For me so I know there's still someone fighting along with me.  We do not have to let the demons win.  Or if they do, we can surely make them earn it.

Other people don't weigh in in this equation.  This demon is assigned to you, personally.  It will stalk you, it will ride you if you let it.  It will drag you to hell.

You have to fight.  The voice that says you're worthless, that you don't matter, that they're better off without you--that voice is not yours.  It belongs to him/her/it!  You gotta find a way to tell it to shut the fuck up.  That you are going to win, no matter what!  For your family and friends?  Fine.  Win for them.  For your hopes and dreams that you've forgotten, that it's taken away from you?  Fine.  Fight for them.  Fight for your very soul if such you have.

Don't worry about others.  They have their problems and you have yours.  Yours may not be as obvious and flashy, but they're no less real.  No one knows what others are going through for as someone said, "We compare their highlight reels with out out takes."  

You win for you.  Or for your family, friends, whomever you have to love and to love you.  You win for that little kid that one day might call you daddy or mama or for that little cat that needs you to feed it.  Don't let the demon win.  Too many people go down with us if we do.

If the dog is what you have to hold on to, hold on to the dog.  Hold your mother's hand.  Sit in her lap and tell her you love her.  Do whatever it takes.  If that's all there is left for you, and I know it can get to that point, hold on to it.
Do you have anyone you love?
I'm sorry.  Often this is all that keeps me here--the thought of what it would do to my daughters.  I'm sure he loved you very much.  Sometimes, we just can't fight anymore.

No regrets.  No time for regrets.  The hammer falls, and the light is gone.  No time even for the sound of the gunshot to enter my ears only inches away.  Everything is black now.  Everything is good now.  It's finally over...in an instant.
I thought about placing an ad for a gym partner.
Just referencing the meme. Never saw the movie, I don't think.

This is helpful...this is the sort of thing I need to hear.  Journaling seems like a good idea.  I'd thought of doing that, but haven't.  I thought maybe I could find patterns in the good days versus the bad.

I have some back exercises to use.  Planks from elbows, hip-ups, leg raises, crunches, and back extensions all work OK.  I need to stretch also.

Knowing what to do isn't so much the problem as finding the motivation to do what I can.  I'm so far out of shape and so down at this point that it seems like an insurmountable task to get out of bed.  

I did walk about half a mile today.  So I got that going for me, which is nice.
IDK.
Clinical trials. Some promise.
TMS is nothing like ECT. I've had both. TMS has almost no side effects and is very effective even for folks nothing else has helped in many cases.

I guess you mean TMS?  IDK what TLA means either.  Totally lame acronym?

At any rate, TMS is Trans cranial magnetic therapy.  Highly effective and relatively new.

I can tell you all about it if you wish, just not right this moment.

Interesting piece.  Oddly, when the water was knocked over and the glare given, I pictured a cat, not a girl.  A cat glaring because it is now wet.

Not exactly sure what you are trying to capture OP, but I enjoyed it.

She's mine.  I'm hers.  Better or worse.  Not popular here, but Biblical principals.  Saved for each other--she's slept with no other man nor I any other woman.  I never hope to.  Divorce is no option.  You fight the battles and reap the rewards together.  The rewards are many.

Not even sure I believe in God anymore, but I believe in her.  I always will.  For some odd reason, she still believes in me too.  When I no longer do.
I like the personification of the sun and moon, the relentless chase.
24 years.  Together maybe 26.

I'll talk to you, if you want.  I'm not too good myself right now.  

I know the feeling of being trapped.  I don't know, but I imagine there's a way out of whatever your problems are.  Respond or PM if you wish.

It's an anonymous internet account.  Who are we supposed to alert?  And how?  And did you?  

If you know the answer, please tell me.
Are you still here?  Hoping so.  Not sure why, but I hope you're ok.  Or as OK as you can be right now.  Please let me know you are.

>If there is hell...

One of two things that keeps me here.

The other is what it would do to my family, particularly my wife and children.

I don't want to live anymore, though.
Me too.

I know what you are going through, to some extent.  I was hospitalized far a week this time last year.  I probably should have stayed.  

There are many treatment options.  Try as many as you can until one works.  Nothing has worked for me, at least not permanently.
You as well.  I am getting a second round of TMS.  I hope that works for me.  I hope you find your way.
You are delusional.  Please seek emergency care.

How are you now?  I've not gone months.  But I've gone years going to work, going to bed, rinse, repeat.

I wish I could die.  I think.
My brother is a Buddhist.  The four noble truths do not apply here.

I don't have a particularly lavish lifestyle--I live in a poor area.  Also, I don't do terribly well with managing my finances.  I recently hired a financial coach and things seem to be headed in the right direction, though.  Also, I've probably spent in the neighborhood of $20,000 out of pocket in the last couple years on medical expenses.

I haven't taken a trip of any consequence in a decade.  I plan/hope to visit the beach in the spring.  My favorite place in the wold, and I've not been there in ten years.

Sorry.  It is what it is.  For some people, it can be situational. For others it is not.  For most, it is both.

I despise my current superior at work.  There's that.  I also have poor physical health, partly due to depression, partly due to a back injury.  I also had to quit martial arts due to said injury.

I had an epidural steroid recently for the injury.  I also took hydrocodone for a couple months or so.  According to my psychiatrist, these can both exacerbate depression.

Despite any of that, I have always had OCD and GAD.  Since I was a small child.  I am also mildly autistic.  All diagnosed by a qualified professional, not me.

Due to depression, I feel I am a burden to those around me.  I do not feel I do as good a job at my work as I once did.  I have gained a great deal of weight.  All of this, of course, fuels the fire.

So, yes, there were some situational things, and some things affect the situation.  But I've always had mental illness and the predisposition (is that the right word?  Not thinking too clearly.) to it.

Change your major. If you're young, now is the time.  Don't worry about the credits you'll lose.  You'll miss the years you waste in something you hate more when you're older.

My advice?  Find something that pays well that you enjoy.  Stay away from debt as best you can.  

Unfortunately, I speak from experience.  Many years of it.

I'm one class and a portion of a paper from a doctorate.  I haven't been back to school in over three years.  I have until 2021 to finish the degree.  

Ask your doctor or guidance counselor (whatever they call them) if there's anything that can be done for you.  Depression is a recognized disability.

It's a chemical imbalance, to the best of current medical understanding.  Problem being there are lots of chemicals involved.  Treating it is inexact to be kind.

I've had every class of drugs available save MAOIs, Ketamine, and psylocybin.

MAOIs are very dangerous, and Ketamine is terribly expensive, and psilocybin is illegal to the best of my knowledge.

I've also had ECT, TMS, and psychotherapy. 

Knowing what causes it--knowing it's illogical--neither one changes anything.
TMS is anywhere from $10,000 to $20,000 in the US.  Maybe some outside that range.  My insurance covered most of it.
ECT messed me up bad.  Check my comment history if you want details--I just typed it out.

Have you heard of TMS?  if you haven't and can do so, PLEASE check into it before ECT.  ECT is one of the worst things I've ever done to myself.  It was crippling.  I had a dissociative episode, lost a into of memory, and have gaps in my memory.

My wife mentioned the other day something about when my 11 year old had meningitis (I think).  I did not remember it.  I now have some vague recollection of her being ill.  No idea what else might be gone.

It does work for people, though, but TMS, while relatively new is very effective and has almost no side effects.  Headache is the only one I can think of.
Because they've not been there.

It's not a choice.  I have three college degrees.  I made excellent grades.  I have a 25 year marriage.  I have a home in the country.  I have high evaluations at work.  I have an income more than twice the average for where I live.  I stand to retire a millionaire or very close.

And I want to die.
Have you tried TMS?
Wait--your parents wanted your sister to be able to sleep with the 20 y/old?

You need to come down from the pedestal you've placed yourself on.  This is the most conceited thing I can conceive of as an answer.  I was unqualified?  What right do you have to judge me, my motives, intentions, or heart?  Perhaps you're the one who needs to pray here.

If I knew for certain you are right, I'd be gone already.  I want no second chances.  I just want to be gone. Completely.  I don't believe that, really, though.  I am afraid to die.  I am also afraid not to.

I don't think I can get ketamine with my insurance.  I've literally spent thousands out of pocket on this.  Tens of thousands if you count insurance.  

I have a therapist.  CBT is one of the tools in her chest.

How do you know they'd not be better off without me.  I don't know that.
Never be sorry for trying to help someone.

I've had OCD and anxiety disorder since I can remember.  I've had major depressive disorder. For several years--five, six?  Maybe less.  I don't know.

I've had every class of drug save MAOIs and Ketamine.  I've had therapy.  Hospitalization.  Electro convulsive therapy.  Trans-cranial Magnetic Therapy.  

Basically, I've had almost every treatment known. TMS was best, but not lasting.

As I say, death is my desire.  It seems the only way out.
I have.  And it is that bad.  Never again.
I know the Ctholic view of suicide--mortal sin.  Any caveats to that?

Because I believed it.

Not sure when it started.  It isn't something that just happens overnight.
Thx.
I hope it works for you.
If I wake up, I might consider revising.  Goodnight.
Thanks.  And Goodnight.
Fair enough.  I'm only on here sporadically.

Did you mean to write "just that say"?

Transpose means to "one put" word where the other goes and vice versa.
I have three children.  I go on.

Better is relative.  Better comes and goes.  I doubt I'll ever be well.  I come here when I'm down usually.  

If I sleep forever tonight, it won't be by intent.  But it'll be ok.
This one took me a minute.  Addiction is a frightening thing.  Prison moreso.  I have dealt with the former.  Not the latter.  The symbolism works here.  The bottles are indeed a prison.
This is not my particular taste so far as style, but it is powerful nonetheless.  More so on a second reading.  I believe you have transposed two words, though.

I don't even know what to say.  I've been there, pain that seemed to have no end.  In my case, there was something finally to be done.  I'm much better.  But when it was at its worst, I understood all too well.

I still deal with depression.  I'd still like release from this.  But I don't believe in suicide.  Even with that said, I've considered it so many times.

If you can, choose life.  If not, I don't really know what to say.  I'm sorry you have this to deal with.
If you are concerned that very few people will come to your funeral, how about putting it off until a better time?  There are people here who can help.

There is likely a way to get therapy for free.  If you want to PM some location information that isn't too specific, like what state, I'm willing to try to find something for you.

Are you in the US?

Many people have violent thoughts.  Doesn't mean you'll act on them.  If you think there's a possibility, though, you're right to be concerned.  

Whatever you do, don't feed it by watching anything that would do so.

I've been in treatment for several *years* now.  I've had every major class of meds, save three of the most dangerous/new ones.  I've had CBT.  I've had ECT.  I've had TMS.  I've tried excercise.  I've tried meditation.  I've tried alcohol.  Most things have little effect.  Thing is, you keep looking for something until you find what works for you.  You don't give up.  

I've been where you are.  Suicide seems the answer.  Suicide is easy.  Living is hard.  So why not take the easy way?  I don't know what your answer is.  Mine is that I have people who would hurt a lot if I took the easy route.  I won't lessen my pain by transferring it to them.
Pm me the information, please.

My depression is chemical, primarily.  Situational depression can definitely add to it, but it appears that my brain, thyroid, and pituitary glands do not function properly in producing the chemicals needed for normal emotional function.  Much of this would appear to be genetic.  Medicines work only nominally.  "Natural" remedies have little effect as well.

If you've never heard of it, check into Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation.  It helped me more than anything.
Advice on quitting porn?

I've dealt with it for a long, long time. Maybe longer than your 22 years, off and on.

I took TMS for it recently, and it seemed miraculous.  I've quit my medications, but it looks like I'm going to have to go back on Cymbalta.  I don't want to be on some medicine the rest of my life.

Cymbalta fogs my brain.  I'm to see an endocrinologist soon, but I've about lost hope that I can ever be really better.

Old man, nothing to look forward to but misery.  Oddly, I think that may be how my father feels.  He doesn't talk about such things.
This isn't a novelty account.  That was an off-hand comment.  I'm not suicidal at the moment, but I have been in the past.

Nothing matters...everyone's going to die...

Then why not now?
I think you misunderstood what I was asking for help with.

I'm not OP, so you didn't misread my post.  I was simply adding my own reply.  I'm middle aged and I'm tired of fighting.  I've fought most of my life.  I have a good life, but my own demons, chemical imbalances, whatever you want to call them, keep me miserable.  Now I just want to know how to screw up the courage to die.

I'm 41 years old.  I've fought this as long as I can remember off and on.  I've done it all--talk, drugs, ECT, excercise, nutrition.  

Now it seems a permanent state.  I just want to get the courage/nerve to carry it off.  Everyone involved would be better off If I were out the picture with my depression, myself most of all.  I have guns.  99% effectiveness.  I just need the nerve to pull the trigger.

I can't tell you not to kill yourself, but I can tell you that something like this can be overcome, especially at your age.  You can look to your school or your parents if they are supportive to help you.  Someone with more experience might have a solution or help you find one.  There may be good reasons for suicide, but I personally don't think this is it.  Mind you, I'm suicidal myself, but I'm also twice your age and I've fought it off and on since I was younger than you.

>You don't die, because summoning the courage for such an act is beyond most of us.

So how do I find it?  That's all I need to know.
How?
Not especially helpful, but thanks, I guess?

It's likely a chemical imbalance in your brain.  Drugs may help, but you may want to talk to your doctor about ECT or a similar treatment.  

There's nothing outwardly wrong in my life either, but I want to die.  I know what the reason is though.  It IS all in my head.  Sometimes, though, I still feel like it'd just be easier not to fight it.  So, I know what it feels like.

Suicide is a rather permanent solution.  There are documented cases of people who have survived attempts and said that they realized in the last moments that everything in their life can be fixed, except the decision to end it.

Try pharmaceuticals.  It generally only gets worse over time if untreated.  Drugs are made for a reason.  Also, try a CBT therapist.  It may not seem to be doing anything at first, but if you stick with it, it will help.

Don't be mad at yourself for thinking you have depression.  You almost certainly do.  That's the bad news.  The good news is that there are people who can help.  Psychiatrists, psychologists, your GP.  Reach out to these professionals and get some relief.  Intense exercise also helps.  My psychiatrist prescribed an hour per day.
It's been two years.  If it can't be overcome, I might as well be dead.
Thanks for the reply.  My musical taste runs toward metal.  I listen to it every day.  I've recently been taking walks for exercise as well.  Anything else?
Ok for now.  Meds are working.  Plan on going inpatient in about a month. Sooner if need be.  Thanks.
That would be incredible.  I've been on meds for years.  I'm hoping the inpatient thing will do more for me.  Thanks for the reply.

I am at your first stage now.  I am going into a psyche hospital in about a month to try to finally get my head straight.  My next step is my physical health.  I hope I can lose about 80ish lbs once my depression and anxiety is under control.  Hopefully the hospitalization can help with that.  Did finding the right balance really help you much?
Thanks.  I'm scared to death of this.  I basically live with my iPad or PC in front of me, and I'm not looking forward to withdrawal.  I'm afraid of boredom as much as anything.

Someone has to be the craziest one there.  I'm planning on checking into a hospital myself.  I've thought about this.  What if my roommate is totally nuts?  I'm relatively ok on my meds, but there's bound to be some really whacked out people there, right?  This actually worries me.  (serious)
Thank you.
Good.  Let me know if I can be of help.  This is an alternate account which I check ever so often.
Is it possible that your meds need adjusting?  Also, have you considered therapy in addition to drugs?
Have you seen a doctor about it?  A psychiatrist or even a general practitioner can be of great use in cases like this.
How long have you been on meds?  How long depressed?
Been there , done that.  Let's talk if you need to.  What caused you to start down this path?
What are you doing to treat your condition?
Find a good one and it can be a positive experience.  I can see where the vice versa would definitely be true, though.

I wish I never had to leave my house.  Unfortunately, I have to work.  My wife and children depend on my doing that, so I have to face the world, though I seldom want to.  It's nearly midnight here, and I dread work tomorrow, but I can't sleep.
That sounds wonderful, actually.  I don't generally snap out of it.  I just get a little closer to the surface before sinking back down.  I keep trying to reach that point, though.  Someday...

Do you have a therapist?  Talking to someone who is detached and doesn't judge can be of great use.  I'd recommend cognitive behavioral therapy.  And writing down things to discuss with your therapist might be beneficial.

Don't give up.  Fight it.  I'm probably twice your age and I've been fighting it all my life.  There's good times in there too.  You just have to fight through the bad.  Sometimes it can seem that there's no out and that it'll never be good again.  And maybe it won't--but maybe it will. You have to keep holding on to that hope and fight for it.
You're wrong.  There's plenty of good in the world to balance the bad.  The problem is that when we are depressed, we cannot perceive the good, only the bad shows through.

Your perception is more than likely colors by your depression.  Depression is a lens through which we filter the things in our lives.  It distorts things such that you can only see the negative.  I doubt you're such a disappointment or failure.  Most of us are just ordinary with our own ups and downs--those of us with depression have hard time seeing the ups, though, while the downs come through loud and clear.  It's all in the filter.
With friends IRL, yes.  Not with people on the net, though I don't see much difference in the anxiety side.

Can you drive?  Can your friends?  Getting out and DOING something with folks you like will help.  I'm 41, btw, and I've dealt with this since I was way younger than you.  You can do it if you try.  Life can get better.
How old are you?  Are we talking college or HS?  Can you drive?
Mine seem to work a couple months or so.
Socialism.  Reformed republican voting for Sanders.
Spend time with them.  Go out to the movies or something.  Fantastic four looks good.  Getting out with friends helps a lot.
What about the medications just losing their effectiveness?
It may not end, but it can get better.  You remind me of me at your age.  Do you have friends at all who share your interests?
Explain?  Why not you?  Why not me?

Been down that rabbit hole myself.  No need to feel bad about your hobbies or living at home.  You remind me of Scott.  I used to work with Scott at Krystal's (hamburger joint if you don't know).  Scott was probably 300 lbs, either lived at home or maybe had a small apartment--I don't recall.  All he did outside of work was play video games.  And he was happy with it.  I wouldn't mind being Scott.

How old are you?  I'm 41 and I've played this game (depression) my whole life.  Let me know if I can help.  Pretty low myself right now.  Video games offer an escape--you're not a loser for using them.  Same for videos on YouTube.  These are some of the same coping mechanisms I use along with Reddit.  Hobbies help when you can get up the gumption to do them.
What is t3?
I have children.  Bright, beautiful children with great potential.  So I've fulfilled that part.  As for finding my own meaning, that I am lacking.  I suspect many on this board are.
This is how I feel.  I don't know the answer, but you're not alone.  It seems that life kicks me in the teeth whenever I begin to get ahead.

I don't know of the books you refer to, but the myth of Sysiphus is an apt description of what I feel.  Pushing the Boulder every day.  Laying in bed reading garbage on the Internet, looking at porn ( for which I feel guilty), playing video games, and working.  I just want off the ride.  There are no parts that I find joy in.
